newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU declines comment on French privatisation plans.
newsitem.headline: EU declines comment on French privatisation plans.

text.p: EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert declined to comment on Thursday about the prospect that the privatisation of France Telecom and Credit Lyonnais might be delayed, saying it was not a Commission problem whether a company was public or private.
But he expressed concerns about successive delays by the French government in presenting a fresh restructuring plan for Lyonnais.
"Whether you have a privatisation or part privatisation is none of our business," Van Miert said.

He was replying to questions about whether a delay in selling off France Telecom could harm France's chances of meeting a January 1, 1998 deadline for opening up the European telecommunications market to full competition.
On Lyonnais the question was whether a delay would compromise the restructuring of the troubled French bank, which has been through a major slimming course since July 1995.
A new restructuring plan was promised in September, when the Commission agreed to emergency aid which helped the bank post a small half-year profit.
This was achieved by softening the terms of a 135-billion-franc loan Lyonnais had to grant to a state-owned company charged with restructuring the bank's loss-making assets.

Under the plan still to be submitted to the Commission, the new terms will be confirmed beyond 1996. But Van Miert warned that the fresh plan must arrive soon so that the issue "was sorted out before October".
The plan, which also involves the privatisation of Lyonnais, is ready, but was put on hold after the French government called early general elections.

French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin, whose party came out on top in the first round of the elections on Sunday, said early this week he would call off the privatisation of France Telecom. He has since nuanced his position.
The outgoing government planned to sell a 30 to 35 percent stake in a first share offer and pledged to keep 51 percent of the telecoms operator.
